name: Tech Mahindra (Associate Software Engineer)
tagline: Aptitude, essay, technical, psychometric and communication tests

overview.about: Tech Mahindra hires freshers for software engineering roles through campus and off-campus drives. Recent drives report an aptitude + essay test, a technical + psychometric test and an AI-evaluated communication test, followed by technical and HR interviews. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.
eligibility: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech/MCA (some drives include B.Sc/BCA) from eligible batches
Typically 60% or more in 10th, 12th and graduation (as reported)

pattern.note: Essay of ~200 words on one of 2–3 topics

overview.frequency: Campus drives in season; off-campus roles on the careers portal

cards.title: Aptitude coverage
cards.body: Standard quant (percentages, ratios, time-work, speed, P&C), logical (series, coding-decoding, blood relations, puzzles) and verbal (grammar, RC, vocabulary). Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Essay
cards.body: One topic picked from two or three, roughly 200 words. Graded on grammar, structure and clarity.

cards.title: Essay plan in 2 minutes
cards.body:
Topic: 'Remote work — boon or bane?'
Intro: define + stance. Para 1: benefit with example. Para 2: challenge with example. Conclusion: balanced view, one line on the future.

cards.title: Word budget
cards.body: 200 words ≈ 4 short paragraphs of 50 words. Count lines, not words: about 10–12 words per line in most editors.

cards.title: Logical sample
cards.body: Q: Find the missing term: 4, 9, 25, 49, ?, 169 → squares of primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 → 121.

cards.title: Common essay mistakes
points: No paragraph breaks
Repeating the topic sentence
Informal language ('gonna', 'u')
Going far over the word limit

notes.p: Tech Mahindra's fresher assessment is reported to include **aptitude** (quantitative, logical reasoning, verbal), an **essay writing** section, **technical MCQs**, a **psychometric test** and, in some drives, a **coding** section, followed by a communication assessment and interviews. Each part can be an elimination stage. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

**Quant.** A shopkeeper buys 12 pens for ₹100 and sells 10 pens for ₹100. Profit%? CP per pen = 100/12, SP per pen = 10. Profit = (10 − 8.33)/8.33 = **20%**.

**Quant.** Speed of a boat in still water 15 km/h, stream 3 km/h. Time to go 36 km upstream? 36/12 = **3 hours**.

**Logical.** If in a code 'TEACHER' is 'VGCEJGT', how is 'SCHOOL' written? Each letter +2 → **UEJQQN**.

**Logical.** Five people in a row: A is left of B, C is right of B, D is between A and B, E is at the extreme right. Order: **A D B C E**.

**Verbal.** Fill in: 'She is good ___ mathematics.' → **at**.

The essay is typically a short opinion essay on a general topic in limited time. It is graded for grammar, structure, relevance and vocabulary, often by software first. Aim for clear paragraphs and zero spelling errors.

**Four-part structure:** introduction with your view → reason 1 with an example → reason 2 or counter-point with an example → conclusion with a suggestion.

**Sample introduction** for 'Should coding be taught in schools?': 'Coding teaches children how to break problems into steps, a skill useful far beyond computers. For this reason, basic coding should be part of the school curriculum, taught alongside, not instead of, core subjects.'
Common mistakes:
points: Writing a list of points instead of connected paragraphs.
Going under the word limit or far over it.
Copying phrases from memorised essays that do not fit the topic.
Ignoring a section because it seems easy — each part may have a cut-off.

notes.p: Use your time well:
points: Quant: do formula-based questions first (percentages, profit, TSD, interest).
Logical: coding-decoding and series are fast; long puzzles last.
Verbal: grammar and vocabulary in seconds; RC questions after skimming.
Essay: spend 2 minutes planning, most of the time writing, 2 minutes proofreading.
Do not leave questions blank if there is no negative marking in your drive.

notes.p: **Topic: 'Work from home vs work from office.'** Introduction: both models have value; a hybrid approach often works best. Body 1: home working saves commute time and helps focus on deep work. Body 2: office time builds mentoring and team relationships, especially for freshers. Conclusion: teams should agree on fixed office days for collaboration and flexible days for focused work.
Remember:
points: Aptitude, essay, technical, psychometric (+ coding in some drives).
Profit% on CP; upstream speed = u − v.
Essay: intro, two body paragraphs, conclusion.
Proofread every sentence before submitting.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Technical MCQ topics
points: C/Java output questions
OOP, data structures basics
DBMS & SQL
OS & networking fundamentals
Software engineering basics (SDLC, testing)

cards.title: SDLC basics
cards.body: Waterfall: sequential phases. Agile: short iterations (sprints) with continuous feedback. Testing levels: unit → integration → system → acceptance.

cards.title: Sample MCQ
cards.body:
Q: Which data structure gives O(1) average lookup by key?
A hash table (HashMap / dict).

cards.title: Psychometric test
cards.body: A personality questionnaire on how you work, collaborate and handle pressure. Reported as non-eliminatory but can inform later rounds. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Psychometric approach
cards.body: Answer honestly and consistently; don't overthink each statement.

cards.title: Testing sample
cards.body: Q: Testing individual functions in isolation is called? Unit testing. Testing the combined modules together? Integration testing.

cards.q: Testing individual functions in isolation is called:
cards.explain: Unit tests check the smallest testable parts.

notes.p: Technical MCQs are reported to cover **C/C++/Java basics**, **data structures**, **DBMS/SQL**, **operating systems**, **computer networks** and sometimes **software engineering**. Questions are mostly direct concept checks and short output predictions. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

**Q1.** Which data structure is used for BFS? **Queue**.

**Q2.** Worst-case time of quicksort? **O(n²)**.

**Q3.** Which SQL clause filters groups? **HAVING**.

**Q4.** Which layer of OSI does a router work at? **Network layer**.

**Q5.** Which SDLC model suits changing requirements? **Agile**.

**Q6.** Output of this Python snippet:

`nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
print(sorted(set(nums)))
print(nums.index(1), nums.count(1))
print("-".join(str(x * 2) for x in nums if x > 2))`

Output:
`[1, 3, 4, 5]
1 2
6-8-10`

The psychometric test is a long personality questionnaire (often 70–100+ statements). You rate how much you agree or choose the statement most like you. It checks work-related traits: **teamwork, reliability, stress handling, openness to learning, integrity**. There are no right answers, but your answers should be **consistent** — the same idea appears several times in different wording.
points: Answer as you genuinely behave at work or in college projects.
Stay consistent; contradictions lower your profile.
Avoid always choosing the extreme option.
Do not try to guess what the company 'wants' on every item — it shows as inconsistency.
Keep a steady pace; there is usually a time limit.

notes.p:
**'I prefer to finish my own tasks before helping teammates.'** A balanced professional answer is usually near neutral — you complete your work but help others when needed.

**'I get upset when plans change suddenly.'** Disagreeing slightly fits roles that need adaptability; answer honestly.

**'I sometimes take credit for others' work.'** Integrity items like this are designed to catch faking; answer truthfully.

**Q7.** Which normal form removes transitive dependencies? **3NF**.

**Q8.** Which scheduling algorithm can cause starvation? **Priority scheduling** (and SJF); fixed with aging.

**Q9.** In Java, which keyword prevents a method from being overridden? **final**.

**Q10.** Time complexity of binary search? **O(log n)**.

**Q11.** Which protocol assigns IP addresses automatically? **DHCP**.

**Q12.** What does the `static` keyword on a Java method mean? It belongs to the class, so it can be called without an object.
Common mistakes:
points: Rushing technical MCQs and confusing similar terms (HAVING vs WHERE, TCP vs UDP).
Answering psychometric items inconsistently.
Changing answer style halfway through the long questionnaire because of fatigue.
Skipping the coding section if your drive includes one.

notes.p: Remember:
points: Technical MCQs: DS, DBMS, OS, CN, SDLC, language basics.
BFS uses a queue; HAVING filters groups; routers are layer 3.
Psychometric: honest, consistent, not extreme.
Integrity questions catch faking.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Communication test
cards.body: Short AI-evaluated tasks: read aloud, repeat sentences, answer simple questions. Speak clearly at a steady pace in a quiet room.

cards.title: Technical interview
cards.body: Project, OOP, SQL, a program (e.g. reverse a string, factorial, prime check), and maybe questions on technologies listed in your resume.

cards.title: HR interview
cards.body: Tell me about yourself, why Tech Mahindra, willingness to relocate and work in shifts, career goals.

cards.title: Typical program
cards.body:
Check prime efficiently:
def is_prime(n):
    if n < 2: return False
    i = 2
    while i * i <= n:
        if n % i == 0: return False
        i += 1
    return True

cards.title: Explain complexity
cards.body: After writing the prime check, say: 'O(√n) because any factor above √n pairs with one below it.' Small touches like this lift a fresher interview.

cards.title: Be careful with offers
cards.body: Tech Mahindra warns about fake job offers. Genuine processes never ask for payment; verify on the official careers portal.

cards.q: Time complexity of trial division up to √n for primality:
cards.explain: The loop runs while i² ≤ n.

cards.q: A message asks you to pay a 'registration fee' for a Tech Mahindra offer. You should:
options: Pay quickly to secure the seat
Treat it as fraud and verify on the official careers portal
cards.explain: Genuine recruiters do not charge fees.

notes.p: Tech Mahindra commonly runs a **communication assessment** — an automated spoken-English test with tasks like reading aloud, repeating sentences, sentence building, answering short questions and passage retelling — before the **technical** and **HR interviews**. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.
points: Speak clearly at a natural pace; clarity matters more than accent.
Use a quiet room and a working headset.
In repeat tasks, keep going even if you miss a word.
Practise by reading news aloud for 10 minutes daily.

notes.p:
**Q: What is the difference between C and C++?** A: C is procedural; C++ adds classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, templates and the STL.

**Q: What is a virtual function?** A: A base-class function that can be overridden so the call is decided at runtime based on the actual object.

**Q: What is a foreign key?** A: A column referencing another table's primary key to keep data consistent.

**Q: Explain the OSI model briefly.** A: Seven layers — physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, application — each handling one part of communication.

**Q: Write a program to swap two numbers without a third variable.** A: `a = a + b; b = a - b; a = a - b;` (or XOR swap; watch overflow).

**Q: Why Tech Mahindra?** A: Mention its strong telecom and digital transformation work, fresher training and your interest in those areas, with one fact from the official site.

**Q: How do you handle pressure?** A: Prioritise, break work into steps, communicate early — with a short example.

**Q: Are you willing to sign a service agreement and relocate?** A: Read the terms beforehand and answer honestly.

**Q: What motivates you?** A: Learning new technologies and seeing users benefit from what you build.
Before the interview day:
points: Revise your resume line by line.
Practise a 1-minute self-introduction aloud.
Revise OOP, DBMS, OS and networks basics.
Prepare two STAR stories (teamwork, challenge).
Check camera, mic and internet for online rounds.

notes.p: Avoid these in Tech Mahindra interviews:
points: Memorised answers that sound robotic — speak naturally.
Not knowing what is written in your own resume.
Vague answers to 'why Tech Mahindra' without any specific fact.
Arguing with the interviewer instead of explaining your reasoning calmly.
Saying 'I don't know' and stopping — explain how you would find the answer instead.
Poor audio or video setup in online rounds; test everything 30 minutes early.

notes.p: Remember:
points: Communication test → technical → HR.
Clear, steady speech beats fast speech.
Know virtual functions, keys, OSI, swap logic.
Specific reasons for Tech Mahindra.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.
